Piper Sandler upgraded $KTOS to Overweight and raised its price target to $75. The analyst cited clearer near-term growth driven by the MACH-TB hypersonic test program, increasing turbojet and turbofan production rates, and potential new tactical drone opportunities. The firm’s valuation now appears better aligned with multi-year expectations for the Marine Corps’ CCA program and MUX TACAIR. Recent contract awards and funding signals have also increased confidence in the company’s revenue pipeline, even with a likely continuing resolution at the start of fiscal 2027. The upgrade reflects growing visibility into $KTOS’s role in affordable unmanned systems and propulsion technologies supporting next-generation defense needs.

$RKLB Rocket Lab has won a $397 million U.S. Space Force contract to develop, launch on Neutron, and operate multiple Flatellites under the SB-AMTI program. These flat-stackable satellites carry sensors and high-bandwidth links to deliver real-time tracking of aircraft and missile threats from orbit. The system is designed to provide persistent coverage in contested areas where traditional surveillance aircraft face high risk. The award highlights Rocket Lab’s end-to-end model—building the spacecraft, flying them on its own medium-lift rocket, and running the mission from secure facilities. It also gives Neutron its first publicly disclosed payload commitment from a major defense customer. Combined with other recent Space Force wins, this strengthens the company’s position as a reliable supplier of proliferated, resilient space architecture for national security.
